tagline: Aalto University's speech recognition group, whose open Morfessor and AaltoASR tools have long supported speech and language technology for morphologically rich languages.
about: The speech recognition group sits in the Department of Information and Communications Engineering at Aalto University in Espoo and is part of the Finnish Center for Artificial Intelligence. It works on acoustic modeling of phonemes, statistical language models for large-vocabulary continuous speech recognition, and speech technology for under-resourced languages.

The group publishes its research software through the aalto-speech GitHub organization, created in 2013. The best known repositories are Morfessor, a tool for unsupervised and semi-supervised morphological segmentation, AaltoASR, a set of recognition tools, and speaker diarization scripts built on that toolkit.

Professor Mikko Kurimo heads the group and is known internationally for unsupervised subword modeling for languages with rich word inflection, such as Finnish, Estonian, Turkish and Arabic. The software mainly serves other speech and language researchers.
mission: The group aims to improve speech recognition with new algorithms and to make recognition practical for languages with limited data and heavy inflection. It shares its tools openly so that other researchers can reuse and extend them.

tagline: AdapterHub maintains the open Adapters library, a modular, parameter-efficient fine-tuning toolkit built on Hugging Face Transformers.
about: AdapterHub began in 2020 as a framework for sharing and composing adapters, small sets of added weights that stand in for full fine-tuning of a pretrained model. The original paper by Pfeiffer and colleagues was presented at EMNLP 2020, and the GitHub organization was created in April 2020.

In November 2023 the project released the unified Adapters package, replacing the earlier adapter-transformers fork, with a library paper at EMNLP 2023. The library is released under the Apache 2.0 licence and had about 2,800 GitHub stars in 2026.

Version 1.2.0, announced in May 2025, added a plugin interface for attaching adapter functionality to nearly any Transformer model. The project is run by researchers associated with TU Darmstadt and serves practitioners who need to adapt large models cheaply.
mission: AdapterHub aims to make parameter-efficient and modular transfer learning easy to use, share and combine. It treats adapters as reusable components that the community can publish and compose.

tagline: The AI Laboratory at the University of Latvia builds open Latvian language resources, from the Tezaurs lexicon to a multilayer corpus and Latvian BERT models.
about: The Artificial Intelligence Laboratory belongs to the Institute of Mathematics and Computer Science at the University of Latvia in Riga and has conducted research since 1992. Its work covers natural language processing and machine learning, including Latvian speech recognition and synthesis, syntactic and semantic analysis and language models.

The lab maintains a set of public Latvian resources, among them Tezaurs.lv, Korpuss.lv, the LV-PIPE tools, CLARIN-LV and Balsutalka.lv. Its FullStack-LV repository offers a multilayer corpus with Universal Dependencies, FrameNet, PropBank and AMR layers, released under a Creative Commons licence.

Funding comes from the European Union, the European Regional Development Fund and Latvian ministries and councils. The lab has partnered with the news agency LETA, Deutsche Welle and the National Library of Latvia.
mission: The lab states that it develops resources and technologies that help Latvian thrive in a multilingual environment. It publishes its tools and data openly for researchers and developers.

tagline: The AI and Machine Learning Lab at TU Darmstadt releases open safety tooling and reasoning research, including LlavaGuard and Safe Latent Diffusion.
about: The AIML Lab at TU Darmstadt is led by Professor Kristian Kersting, who joined the university in 2019 and also co-directs hessian.AI. Its stated aims are advancing statistical learning, probabilistic reasoning and collaborative intelligence, with work in statistical relational AI, generative modeling and trustworthy machine learning.

The lab publishes code on GitHub and models on Hugging Face, where it lists 20 models and 42 datasets. Safety tools include Safe Latent Diffusion, LlavaGuard and QwenGuard, and recent releases cover OlmoLogic reasoning models and the KletterMix German pretraining data.
Its audience is researchers and developers who need open checks for image-text datasets and generative models.
mission: The lab aims to make machines learn about the world rapidly and flexibly, combining logical and probabilistic methods with deep learning. It emphasises trustworthy and safe generative systems.

tagline: Heidelberg language-model company that built sovereign European models and released part of its research as open weights, now being merged into Cohere.
about: Aleph Alpha was founded in 2019 in Heidelberg by Jonas Andrulis and Samuel Weinbach. It raised a 5.3 million euro seed round in 2020, a further 23 million euros in 2021, and in November 2023 announced a large round led by Schwarz Gruppe and the Dieter Schwarz Foundation.

The company sells specialised sovereign language models and solutions to organisations, and also publishes research code, datasets and models. Its Hugging Face organization carries the Kolibri model, a German and English mixture-of-experts model released in October 2026 under Apache 2.0.

In April 2026 Cohere announced that it would acquire Aleph Alpha, and a definitive merger agreement followed in September 2026. The combined company will operate as Cohere, with Heidelberg kept as a research centre, subject to regulatory approval.
mission: The company says it builds specialised sovereign models that give customers control over their data and adapt to their context. Its open releases support German-language and tokenizer research.

tagline: Danish non-profit research and technology institute whose open resources include DaNLP and the ScandEval benchmark, now EuroEval.
about: The Alexandra Institute was established in Aarhus in 1999 by business people, researchers and public representatives to link Danish companies with university IT research. It became an approved technological service provider in 2007 and has been owned by the Aarhus University Research Foundation since 2012.

Its open source work is published on GitHub and Hugging Face. DaNLP collected Danish datasets and models for tagging, named entity recognition, sentiment and hate speech detection, with a NoDaLiDa 2021 paper; the repository was archived in March 2025. The ScandEval benchmark, described in arXiv 2304.00906, later grew into EuroEval.
The institute serves Danish companies and public bodies and works on language technology, evaluation and responsible AI.
mission: The institute applies IT research to the needs of Danish business and society and publishes language resources so that Danish remains well supported in AI.

tagline: Inria Paris research team behind the CamemBERT family of open French language models and work in computational humanities.
about: ALMAnaCH is an Inria team in Paris working on natural language processing and digital humanities. Its members include Benoît Sagot and Djamé Seddah, who are authors of the original CamemBERT paper alongside colleagues from Inria and Sorbonne Université.

CamemBERT, a RoBERTa-based French model released under an MIT licence in 2019, became a widely adopted reference. CamemBERT 2.0 followed in 2024, and CamemBERTa, by Wissam Antoun, Sagot and Seddah, explored data-efficient training. The team's Hugging Face organization lists 92 models and 43 datasets, including biomedical encoders and Gaperon sparse autoencoders.
The models serve researchers, companies and public bodies that need open French and biomedical text processing.
mission: The team builds and shares language models and data for French and historical or specialised text. It treats open release as part of academic practice.

tagline: London-based AI safety organisation that evaluates frontier models for scheming and publishes open evaluation and interpretability work.
about: Apollo Research was founded in 2023 and is led by CEO and co-founder Marius Hobbhahn. Its stated goal is to secure frontier AI systems across development, deployment and governance, with a focus on scheming, where advanced systems covertly pursue misaligned objectives.

In 2023 it presented at the UK AI Safety Summit and advised the Frontier AI Taskforce. In 2024 it tested OpenAI's o1 before release and published early evidence of in-context scheming in frontier models; in 2025 it ran evaluations for major labs and worked with OpenAI on anti-scheming interventions.

In 2026 the organisation became a Public Benefit Corporation, opened a San Francisco office and began building Watcher, an agent monitoring tool. It publishes code on GitHub, including end-to-end sparse dictionary learning.
mission: Apollo aims to reduce the risk of deceptive and misaligned AI through evaluations, interpretability research and governance advice. It works with developers and governments.

tagline: Munich-area audio AI company and maker of the openSMILE toolkit and open speech emotion and age-gender models.
about: audEERING was founded in 2012 as a spin-off of Technical University of Munich research, with Dagmar Schuller, Florian Eyben, Björn Schuller and Martin Wöllmer named as founders in a 2012 report. It is based in Gilching near Munich.

openSMILE began in 2008 at TUM within the EU SEMAINE project. In 2013 audEERING obtained the rights and published version 2.0 under a research licence. The toolkit is free for research and personal use, while commercial users need a licence, so it is source-available rather than fully open.
The company also maintains open repositories on audio machine learning, including the w2v2-how-to guide and wav2vec2-based emotion and age-gender models on Hugging Face.
mission: audEERING develops audio analysis and speech emotion technology and shares research tooling with the scientific community while selling commercial products.

tagline: The AutoML groups of Freiburg and Hannover, creators of auto-sklearn, SMAC3 and Auto-PyTorch.
about: The AutoML groups at the University of Freiburg and Leibniz University Hannover were led by Frank Hutter and Marius Lindauer, with Matthias Feurer and Katharina Eggensperger among close collaborators. The GitHub organization dates from 2014.

Their system auto-sklearn began as a competition entry and won the first international AutoML challenge in 2015 to 2016 and the second in 2017 to 2018. The 2015 NeurIPS paper introduced it, and auto-sklearn 2.0 appeared in JMLR in 2022. SMAC3 and Auto-PyTorch extend the work to Bayesian optimisation and deep learning.
In an August 2026 post the group announced the closure of automl.org after a decade. Hutter now leads Prior Labs and Lindauer's Hannover group has broadened beyond AutoML.
mission: The groups aimed to make machine learning accessible by automating model and hyperparameter selection, and released their tools as open source for the community.

tagline: Tübingen lab studying robustness and human-like vision, known for the Foolbox toolbox and open robustness benchmarks.
about: The Bethge Lab is led by Matthias Bethge, Professor of Computational Neuroscience and Machine Learning at the University of Tübingen and director of the Tübingen AI Center. Its GitHub organization, created in 2014, carries the tagline Perceiving Neural Networks.

The lab released Foolbox in 2017, a Python toolbox for benchmarking adversarial robustness under an MIT licence, and imagecorruptions and a detection robustness benchmark in 2019. It also published work on ImageNet-C robustness and on comparing machine and human vision.
Wieland Brendel, Jonas Rauber and Robert Geirhos appear among its public GitHub members and papers, and its code serves vision and robustness researchers.
mission: The lab seeks to understand how neural networks perceive images and to make them robust and more human-like, releasing benchmarks and tools openly.

tagline: Open scientific collaboration run by Hugging Face and ServiceNow Research that released The Stack and the StarCoder family of code models.
about: BigCode was established in September 2022 as an open scientific collaboration on the responsible development of code language models. It is stewarded by Hugging Face and ServiceNow and has drawn more than 1,100 members.

The Stack is a permissively licensed code dataset with an opt-out process for developers. StarCoder, trained on 1 trillion tokens, followed in May 2023 and StarCoder2 in early 2024. The project also maintains an evaluation harness.
Leandro von Werra of Hugging Face and Harm de Vries of ServiceNow Research co-lead the project. Because two companies host it, its independence is partial.
mission: BigCode aims to develop code language models openly and responsibly, with transparent data governance, community participation and reproducible evaluation.

about: BUT Speech@FIT is the speech and language research group at the Faculty of Information Technology, Brno University of Technology. Its GitHub organization dates from 2019.

The group released VBx, a Bayesian HMM clustering approach to speaker diarization described by Landini, Profant, Diez and Burget, and DiariZen, a pipeline built on pyannote with WavLM-based models. Jan Černocký and Lukáš Burget are co-authors on its diarization system papers.
On Hugging Face the group published csmpt7b, a Czech-focused 7B model, in 2024. Its tools serve speech researchers and diarization challenge participants.
mission: The group advances speech processing and shares open recipes and models, especially for diarization and Czech language technology.

about: Cardiff NLP is a research group at Cardiff University whose GitHub organization was created in October 2020. Jose Camacho-Collados is a prominent member and an author on its flagship benchmark.

TweetEval, presented in Findings of EMNLP 2020, standardises evaluation across tweet classification tasks. The group also released XLM-T and TimeLMs, and the TweetNLP Python platform in 2022, with Twitter-RoBERTa models trained on tens of millions of tweets.
Its models are widely downloaded from Hugging Face and serve researchers and practitioners analysing social media.
mission: The group aims to build language models and evaluation resources that handle the informal, fast-changing language of social media, and to release them openly.

tagline: Aarhus University centre applying NLP to the humanities, behind DaCy, odyCy and the Scandinavian Embedding Benchmark.
about: The Center for Humanities Computing at Aarhus University was set up by the faculty with Kristoffer Nielbo as its first director, and Nielbo later became the first Danish Professor of Humanities Computing. It runs computational infrastructure for humanities researchers.

Its NLP work includes DaCy, a unified Danish pipeline built on spaCy by Kenneth Enevoldsen, Lasse Hansen and Nielbo, odyCy for Ancient Greek, and the Scandinavian Embedding Benchmark co-created with partners.
The centre's GitHub organization has about 188 repositories and its models serve Nordic NLP researchers and humanities scholars.
mission: The centre seeks to make computational methods available across the humanities and to provide open Danish and Scandinavian language tools.

tagline: LMU Munich's language processing centre, behind SimAlign, Glot500 and GlotLID for massively multilingual NLP.
about: The Center for Information and Language Processing at LMU Munich hosts a deep NLP group led by Hinrich Schütze, whose GitHub organization dates from 2017. Its work targets low-resource and multilingual language technology.

SimAlign (2020) is a word alignment tool, Glot500 (2023) scales corpora and models to 500 languages, and GlotLID is a language identification model that covered 1665 languages in its first version and over 2,000 labels in v3.0 as of April 2024.
Authors include Amir Hossein Kargaran, Ayyoob Imani and Schütze, and the data and models are published on GitHub and Hugging Face.

tagline: CLARIN knowledge centre providing open tools, models and corpora for Slovenian, Croatian, Serbian, Bosnian and Montenegrin.
about: CLASSLA was recognised by CLARIN on 19 March 2019. It is operated by CLARIN.SI, the Institute of Croatian Language and CLADA-BG, with hosting at the Jožef Stefan Institute in Ljubljana.

It offers a helpdesk, the CLASSLA-Stanza pipeline for South Slavic languages, with an improved version released in September 2023, and the largest general web corpora for these languages. BERTić, a model for BCMS languages, is described in arXiv 2104.09243.
Recent work includes benchmarks and an LLM evaluation dashboard for South Slavic languages.

tagline: University of Antwerp computational linguistics group, creator of the Pattern web mining library and Dutch NLP resources.
about: CLiPS is the computational linguistics and psycholinguistics research centre at the University of Antwerp, with a GitHub organization created in 2011.
Pattern, by Tom De Smedt and Walter Daelemans, is a BSD-licensed Python package for web mining and NLP with Dutch modules, described in a JMLR 2012 paper. The repository holds about 8,800 stars.
The group also released the multilingual FAQ dataset MFAQ and Dutch embedding models.
mission: CLiPS develops computational models of language and shares software and datasets, with attention to Dutch.

tagline: VU Amsterdam's Computational Linguistics and Text Mining Lab, publishing open Dutch language resources, MedRoBERTa.nl and teaching material.
about: The Computational Linguistics and Text Mining Lab at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam is led by Piek Vossen and Antske Fokkens. It takes part in the Global Wordnet Association and contributes to the Dutch Global Wordnet Grid.
It publishes models, software and resources as open source. MedRoBERTa.nl, introduced in 2021 by Stella Verkijk and Vossen, was pre-trained on nearly 10 million hospital notes from Amsterdam UMC.
The lab's Python for Text Analysis course, created in 2016, has over 450 GitHub stars.
mission: The lab combines computational linguistics and text mining and releases its models, software and teaching resources openly.

tagline: Ugandan AI group building open Luganda and Swahili language models, speech models and datasets on Gemma.
about: Crane AI Labs is a Ugandan group co-founded by Kato Steven Mubiru and CTO Bakunga Bronson. Its Hugging Face organization hosts models, tokenizers and datasets for African languages.

In 2025 it released Ganda Gemma 1B for Luganda and Swahili Gemma 1B, with GGUF and LiteRT builds. In 2026 it added Luganda education assistants, MedGemma-based health models for offline use by rural health workers and ASR models.
Datasets such as UCCB, pedagogy benchmarks and a Luganda tokenizer evaluation support evaluation of low-resource languages.
mission: The group describes its aim as culturally relevant AI for the Global South, delivered on small models that can run on-device.
